answer: Model this as an E11 Modification (conservation treatment is explicitly named in the E11 scope note). E11 < E7 Activity, and P14 carried out by (E7 -> E39) is the necessary property for who carried the activity out; P14.1 in the role of lets several actors be named with different roles on the same activity, since P14 is many-to-many (its own worked example is Michelangelo 'in the role of master craftsman' -- a supervisory role, not a claim he touched every brushstroke). The 2022 SIG thread t1546 revised the P14 scope note precisely to separate active/causal-or-legally-responsible participation (P14) from passive or merely necessary presence, which should instead use P11 had participant. Applying that: the two apprentices did the hands-on filling, regluing and touch-up, so both get P14 carried out by (role: e.g. conservator/assistant carrying out the treatment). The studio principal is recorded on the invoice as having supervised and approved the repairs -- she holds documented professional/legal responsibility for the outcome even without doing the physical work herself, which is exactly the 'causal or legal responsibility' the P14 scope note names and the master-craftsman example models -- so she also gets P14 carried out by, with a distinct P14.1 role (e.g. supervising conservator) from the apprentices. The museum's conservation officer, by contrast, visited twice only to check progress and did none of the hands-on work and held no responsibility for producing the result; per the t1546 clarification her presence is passive/inactive with no causal contribution to the activity, so she should NOT be linked with P14. If her presence is worth recording at all, P11 had participant (or P12 occurred in the presence of) is the correct property, not P14. So: yes, more than one person should be recorded as having carried out the treatment (principal + both apprentices, each P14 with their own P14.1 role), and the conservation officer should be excluded from P14.

rejected_alternatives.option: P14 carried out by for the museum's conservation officer
rejected_alternatives.why_not: t1546 (SIG-agreed scope-note revision by Athanasios Velios, endorsed by Martin Doerr) reserves P14 for active participation with causal or legal responsibility; an actor whose presence is inactive/checking-only without sharing responsibility for the activity should be recorded with P11 had participant instead.

rejected_alternatives.option: Recording only the studio principal as having carried out the work (single carrier)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P14 carried out by is quantified many to many (1,n:0,n) in the concept dossier, and its own canonical example (Michelangelo 'in the role of master craftsman') shows a supervisory carrier being named via P14.1 alongside the possibility of others who did the physical work -- nothing in the property restricts it to one actor.

rejected_alternatives.option: Recording only the apprentices and dropping the principal
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The principal's supervision and formal approval is documented as her responsibility for the outcome, which is the 'causal or legal responsibility' the P14 scope note names as sufficient for P14, distinct from the merely-checking role of the conservation officer.
